views.name: orders_1998
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  orderid AS order_id,
  customerid AS customer_id,
  orderdate AS order_date
FROM orders
WHERE orderdate >= '1998-01-01' AND orderdate < '1999-01-01'
views.description: All orders placed in the year 1998 (order rows filtered to the 1998 date range).

views.name: order_lines_1998
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  od.orderid AS order_id,
  o.customer_id AS customer_id,
  rowid AS order_line_id,
  od.unitprice AS unit_price,
  od.quantity AS quantity
FROM order_details od
JOIN orders_1998 o ON od.orderid = o.order_id
views.description: Order line items for the 1998 orders, joined to their orders so each line is associated with the customer and constrained to 1998; include unit price and quantity for each line (no discounts applied).

views.name: customer_spend_1998
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ol.customer_id AS customer_id,
  SUM(ol.unit_price * ol.quantity) AS total_spend_1998
FROM order_lines_1998 ol
GROUP BY ol.customer_id
views.description: Total 1998 spending per customer computed as the sum over their 1998 order lines of (unit_price * quantity); one row per customer who had at least one 1998 order line.

views.name: spend_group_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cgt.rangebottom AS spending_group_id,
  cgt.groupname AS spending_group_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT cs.customer_id) AS customers_in_group,
  CASE WHEN total.total_customers = 0 THEN 0.0
       ELSE CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT cs.customer_id) AS REAL) / total.total_customers
  END AS percent_of_customers
FROM customergroupthreshold cgt
LEFT JOIN customer_spend_1998 cs
  ON cs.total_spend_1998 >= cgt.rangebottom
  AND cs.total_spend_1998 <= cgt.rangetop
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS total_customers
  FROM customer_spend_1998
) AS total
GROUP BY cgt.rangebottom, cgt.groupname
views.description: Assign each customer to a spending group using the customer group thresholds, then count distinct customers per spending group and include each group's share of the total distinct customers who placed orders in 1998.

views.name: employee_orders
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.employeeid AS employee_id,
  o.orderid AS order_id,
  o.orderdate AS order_date,
  o.requireddate AS required_date,
  o.shippeddate AS shipped_date
FROM orders o
JOIN employees e
  ON o.employeeid = e.employeeid
views.description: All orders attached to each employee (who placed them), including order identifiers and the relevant date fields needed to determine lateness.

views.name: order_lateness_flag
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.employeeid AS employee_id,
  o.orderid AS order_id,
  CASE
    WHEN trim(o.shippeddate) = '' OR o.shippeddate IS NULL THEN 0
    WHEN trim(o.requireddate) = '' OR o.requireddate IS NULL THEN 0
    WHEN date(o.shippeddate) >= date(o.requireddate) THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_late
FROM orders o
views.description: Normalize orders to add a boolean/flag indicating whether each order is late (shipped_date >= required_date) and ensure date fields are canonicalized for comparison.

views.name: employee_order_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  eo.employee_id AS employee_id,
  COUNT(eo.order_id) AS total_orders,
  SUM(CASE WHEN olf.is_late IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE (olf.is_late) END) AS late_orders
FROM
  employee_orders eo
LEFT JOIN
  order_lateness_flag olf
ON
  eo.employee_id = olf.employee_id
  AND eo.order_id = olf.order_id
GROUP BY
  eo.employee_id
views.description: Per-employee aggregated counts: total orders and total late orders (sum of the is_late flag).

views.name: employee_late_rate
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.employeeid AS employee_id,
  COUNT(o.orderid) AS total_orders,
  SUM(CASE WHEN o.shippeddate IS NOT NULL AND o.shippeddate > o.requireddate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_orders,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(o.orderid) = 0 THEN 0.0
    ELSE (SUM(CASE WHEN o.shippeddate IS NOT NULL AND o.shippeddate > o.requireddate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0) / COUNT(o.orderid)
  END AS late_percentage
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN orders o
  ON e.employeeid = o.employeeid
GROUP BY e.employeeid
views.description: Compute per-employee late-order percentage (late_orders / total_orders * 100) and retain employees for downstream filtering/sorting. (This step does not apply the final >50 filter or top-3 limit.)
